A crystal cavern deep beneath the earth, every faceted wall catching the spell's light and fracturing it into a thousand blinding shards, the hum rising to a shriek that shakes the stalactites free.
A standing-stone henge on a chalk hillside at midnight, the great linteled arches flooding with coursing silver fire, the grass between them scorched in geometric patterns no living hand ever drew.

A throne-room where the king himself rises casting, his crown glowing molten, tapestries tearing from the walls, courtiers falling back as the magic reshapes the gilded hall into something ancient and terrible.
A blasted crater left by a previous working, the scorched earth now blazing again as new power floods the old scar, the air above it twisting with heat and residual memory of destruction.
A moonlit cliff over a churning sea, the waves below lit from within by the casting, salt spray igniting as it meets the discharge, the cliff-edge crumbling inch by inch into the roaring dark.

A frozen tundra shrine ringed by ice-carved idols, the permafrost cracking as warmth surges upward through the spell, steam rising in columns between the ancient figures as their blind faces seem to turn.
A sunken coliseum open to a storming sky, the tiered stone seats vibrating, the arena floor splitting along old seams, the crowd of summoned shadows pressed back against the walls by the light.

A forest grove of ancient petrified trees, their stone bark suddenly luminous, the spell moving through them like sap through living wood, every branch-tip flaring briefly before the grove falls utterly, perfectly silent.

An observatory dome thrown open to the stars, the great brass telescope shaking on its mount, star-charts lifting from the table and burning clean, the heavens above visibly shifting in response to the cast.

A submerged sea-temple half-filled with black water, the spell's light turning the water to hammered copper, barnacled statues of drowned gods briefly vivid in the illumination before the walls buckle inward.
A volcanic caldera rim, magma far below already churning, the cast spell descending in a pillar of force that strikes the surface and sends a geyser of liquid fire spiraling into the ashen sky.

A crumbling aqueduct over a gorge, the stone arches suddenly webbed with crackling energy that holds them together even as the spell threatens to unmake everything, the river below fleeing its own channel.

A desert necropolis under a merciless sun gone strange, the sarcophagi trembling in their rows, carved faces lit from within, the sand between them rising in slow columns toward a sky turned bruised green.

A harbor breakwater at high tide, the waves breaking against the stone in sheets of inadvertent fire, the lighthouse beam swallowed by the brighter pulse of the casting, ships at anchor straining their chains.
A glacier's crevasse field at dawn, the blue ice walls catching the magic and deepening it into something colder than cold, fissures opening in silence, the whole frozen mass groaning as if dreaming.

A crossroads shrine at the edge of a dying town, the four painted gods of direction stripped of their paint by the surge, bare wood blazing briefly beautiful, the roads themselves seeming to shift alignment.

An underground aqueduct-turned-cistern, the still black water below the vaulted arches suddenly reflecting a sky that doesn't exist down here, the echo of the casting ringing off curved stone walls without end.

A high mountain monastery courtyard, prayer flags igniting to clean ash, the bronze prayer-wheels spinning without wind, the monks thrown from their feet as the stones beneath them remember being the mountain they were cut from.
